title: Rexx/SQL backend: SQLite with real indexes for ooRexx
summary: Mark Hessling's Rexx/SQL (LGPL) gives ooRexx function-call SQL: SQLCONNECT, SQLCOMMAND, SQLPREPARE/SQLEXECUTE, with results as stem.COLUMN.n. Alchemy uses it through packages/oorexx_rexxsql_backend_v0.1 as a NativeDatabaseBackend (family SQLITE, implementation rexxsql). It exists because NoSQLServer v0.79 and v0.91 look up rows by key with a full table scan; SQLite has b-tree primary and secondary indexes. Rexx/SQL 2.6B3 needed four fixes for ooRexx 5, GCC 14 and its SQLite driver; they are kept as patches for Mark, not as a fork.
invariants: Use RexxSqlSqliteSession~open(path) or SemanticSourceSqliteIndexPlan~open(path); never call SQLCOMMAND directly from store code.
execute(sql) never raises for SQL errors: check result~status (SUCCESS/ERROR) and result~message.
librexxsql.so must be built from upstream/rxsql26B3 plus upstream/patches (tools/build_rexxsql.sh); an unpatched build truncates text at NUL, loses BLOBs and can abort the interpreter.
Credit: Rexx/SQL is Mark Hessling's work; the patches are offered back to him under its licence.
procedure: Qualify: sh run_tests.sh (needs gcc, make, patch, SQLite 3 and ooRexx headers).

provenance.claim: Backend class and its published capabilities.
